question: Why is UCI test accuracy ~0.958 rather than the ~0.97-0.99 reported in published work?
answer: Published figures are computed WITHOUT removing duplicate rows. 5,206 of the 11,055 UCI rows are exact duplicates, so when duplicates are retained a large majority of test rows also appear in the training set. The model can memorise them, which inflates apparent accuracy. De-duplication removes that contamination.
method: Soft-voting ensemble with the tuned UCI hyperparameters, single stratified 85/15 split, seed 42, identical in both arms; the only difference is whether exact duplicate rows were removed before splitting.
conclusion: The lower accuracy is CORRECT and is the honest estimate. It is not a bug upstream. Task 2.3 de-duplication is doing real work: it eliminates train/test contamination that accounts for roughly two accuracy points on this dataset. The de-duplicated figure is the one that should be reported, with this comparison cited as justification.
caveat: De-duplication also shifts the UCI class balance from 44.31% phishing (matching the published figure) to 51.62%, because duplicated rows are not distributed evenly across classes. Both figures are recorded in results/preprocessing_uci.json.
